title: Bribing and signaling in second price auctions
summary_en: Real-world second-price auctions are vulnerable to side payments: a high-value bidder can offer a competitor a bribe to drop out. Eső and Schummer model bribing and signalling in this setting and characterise when communication between bidders pre-bid is destabilising vs. when it is benign. The paper provides a microfoundation for why second-price auctions, despite their textbook revenue-equivalence properties, can perform worse than first-price auctions in environments where pre-bid bidder communication is feasible.
policy_relevance: Direct relevance for Hungarian public-procurement integrity policy (Állami Számvevőszék, Integritás Hatóság, GVH): the paper supports the case for first-price (sealed-bid) over second-price designs in tender environments where pre-bid communication between bidders cannot be reliably prevented — a recurring concern in Hungarian construction and IT-procurement tenders.
